datasets.title: L.A. County Park Needs Assessment Results
datasets.notes: In March 2015, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors approved a motion to initiate the Countywide Comprehensive Parks and Recreation Needs Assessment.  This represents an unprecedented effort to document existing parks and recreation facilities in cities and unincorporated communities and to use these data to determine the scope, scale, and location of park need in Los Angeles County.  The Parks Needs Assessment will help local officials, park agencies, and residents understand the future steps that need to be taken to ensure all communities have adequate access to thriving parks.

datasets.title: COVID-19 Vulnerability and Recovery Index
datasets.notes:
The COVID-19 Vulnerability and Recovery Index uses Tract and ZIP
Code-level data* to
identify California communities most in need of immediate and long-term
pandemic and economic relief. Specifically, the Index is comprised of three
components — Risk, Severity, and Recovery Need with the last scoring the ability
to recover from the health, economic, and social costs of the pandemic.
Communities with higher Index scores face a higher risk of COVID-19 infection
and death and a longer uphill economic recovery. Conversely, those with lower
scores are less vulnerable.

datasets.title: 3rd Graders Meeting or Exceeding California Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy
datasets.notes: Note, information is based on location of the school, not students’ community of residence.   Third grade represents a key transition point for reading proficiency and literacy as children are expected to make the shift from learning-to-read to reading-to-learn. Children found to have low reading skills in the 3rd grade are at increased risk for poor academic outcomes, which can have profound consequences for future health and longevity.  For more information about the Community Health Profiles Data Initiative, please see the  initiative homepage.

datasets.notes: Drinking Water - SAFER Dashboard Failing and At-Risk Drinking Water Systems    Drought is a regional hazard; a community's susceptibility to it is influenced primarily by the status of their water system. Drought impacts water quality because decreasing well water levels lead to increased concentrations of contaminants such as arsenic. datasets.notes: Data are for noninstitutionalized civilian population.  Medi-Cal is California’s Medicaid health insurance program. datasets.title: Poverty Rate 2010
datasets.notes: This data shows countywide poverty rate distribution in 2010. In 2010, countywide poverty rate is 17.2%. In 973 out of 2,344 tracts (41.5%) the rate is higher than county average. The number of tracts in which the rate is two times higher than average rate is 279 (11.9%). Most tracts with poverty rate above average are spread near downtown, East Los Angeles, and South Los Angeles.        Main data fields are:      CT10: 2010 census tract number     Poverty Rate 2010: 2010 poverty rate by 2010 census tracts.

datasets.name: item.html?id=5d1b6dea935a46d0b1f1ad8541999ffa&sublayer=0
datasets.title: Poverty Rate 2019
datasets.notes: This data shows the countywide poverty rate in 2019. The poverty rate in Los Angeles County in 2019 is 13.4%.  Comparing to 17.2% in 2010, there is a drop in the poverty rate, which implies an improvement in poverty status over a decade. In 994 out of 2,344 tracts (42.4%), the rate is higher than county average. However, the number of tracts in which the rate is two times higher than average rate is 206(8.8%) in 2019 whereas 279 (11.9%) in 2010. Most tracts with poverty rate above county average are spread near downtown, East Los Angeles, and South Los Angeles as in 2010 poverty map.

datasets.name: item.html?id=331d5ba7be4442a9b4b678763ab1bb8a&sublayer=0
datasets.title: CDC Social Vulnerability Index
datasets.notes: The tract-level SVI shows the relative vulnerability of the population of every U.S. Census tract. The county-level SVI shows the relative vulnerability of every U.S. county population. The SVI ranks tracts (or counties) on 15 social factors, described in detail in the documentation. The tract (or county) rankings for individual factors are further grouped into four related themes. Thus each enumeration unit receives a ranking for each Census variable and for each of the four themes, as well as an overall ranking.  This layer is based on  https://lacounty.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=cb

datasets.title: LARIAC7 Rooftop Albedo - CT20
datasets.notes: These layers group the 2023 building-level solar albedo (reflectance) of building rooftops to calculate average albedo values at various geographic levels in Los Angeles County. For more information on the building-level dataset and how it was created, please see:  LARIAC7 Rooftop Albedo - Buildings - Overview .  Rooftop reflectivity is an important component of determining "cool" roofs, which contribute to greater energy efficiency, lower energy consumption, and reduction of the urban heat island effect.  Solar Albedo ranges from 0-1 (least to most reflective). An albedo value higher than 0.

datasets.notes: Park Need Study Area information, including the level of need, demographics, and health indicators.   Park need levels were determined as part of our Comprehensive Countywide Park Needs Assessment, completed in 2016.  All demographics are current as of June, 2020.  Health indicators are from CalEnviroScreen's study from 2018.     Demographics include:    Population by Race  Population by Age  Median Household Income  Household Size  Educational Attainment   Health indicators, taken from CalEnviroScreen, include:     Asthma per 10,000  Cardiovascular Disease per 10,000  Low Birth Rate per 10,0
